Business context · user journeys and feature catalog

Validate — Business E2E Map

This map describes the administration portal and tenant-facing capabilities visible in the inspected frontend and backend repositories. The biometric identity decision belongs to external components and is not asserted here.

Overview

Roles, permission boundaries and the highest-risk route from tenant provisioning to operational use.

Validate is a multitenant administration layer for organisations using a separate identity-validation service. A platform administrator provisions tenants and credentials; tenant administrators configure their own resources; tenant application users review tenant-scoped logs; tenant API clients synchronize or validate tenant/device context. The inspected code does not establish the result of a biometric identity check.

Role hierarchy and permissions

PrincipalSystem role / policyPrimary outcomePortal and API access
Platform administratorAdmin / SuperAdminSistemaProvision and administer tenants, platform users, operators, products, settings, logs and ATDP operations.Admin-only routes; system-policy API operations.
Tenant administratorTenantAdmin / SuperAdminTenantManage its tenant's branches, terminals, devices and application users./admin-panel; tenant-scoped resource and log APIs.
Tenant application userUserApp / LogsReview operational logs for its tenant.Tenant log routes and own-log API policies; no resource-management menu.
Tenant API clientTenantApiAuthenticate as a machine, synchronize supported data and validate tenant/device context.Machine API operations; no portal session.

The code identifies TenantApi as a machine principal rather than a person. The frontend human account types are Admin, TenantAdmin and UserApp.

TenantApi is an automated tenant principal, not a human persona.

PermissionsMachine API operations; validation requires a tenant claim. No portal route or email key exists for this principal.
Pain pointsInvalid credentials/tenant claim, encryption failure, or resource context mismatch.
Test identityProvisioned tenant API client credentials; keep values in environment/secret storage and reference names only.
JourneySynchronize and validate tenant/device context.

Journey: Provision, activate and configure a tenant

Risk: high · entry /tenants · actors: Platform administrator, Tenant administrator.

  1. Platform administrator signs in and opens the tenant list. The tenant form captures identity, operator configuration and security settings.
  2. Administrator creates the tenant and uses its detail tabs to manage credentials/secrets and tenant administrators. The service persists tenant settings and encrypts connection credentials.
  3. Tenant administrator receives an activation message, follows a valid token and sets a password. The token is time-limited; activation clears it and the forced-password-change state.
  4. Tenant administrator signs in. A session requiring password change routes to /change-password; otherwise it routes to /admin-panel.
  5. Tenant administrator creates and maintains branches, terminals, devices and application users. CSV import and export are available for supported resource types.
Branch or failureExpected handling / evidenceData/API pointer
Duplicate RNEC or invalid tenant fieldsReject create/update; RNEC is unique. UI schema requires uppercase letters/digits and constrains business name length/characters.business-data-context#flow-tenant-provisioning; tenant.schema.ts; TenantService.
Activation email not deliveredAccount remains created and response warns about delivery; administrator can resend activation.business-data-context#flow-account-activation; TenantAdminService.
Invalid or expired tokenActivation must not complete; runtime message and resend recovery were not verified in a running app.AuthService; activation routes in AuthController.
Tenant inactive or deletedDetail shows inactive warning and disables resource tabs; deleted tenants omit CSV import action.tenant-detail.component.ts; TenantService.
Duplicate resource identityReject conflicting identifiers and preserve tenant ownership/child-protection rules.business-data-context#flow-tenant-resource-management.

Critical path: tenant identity and credentials persist, the admin account activates, and tenant resources can be created without crossing tenant boundaries. Email delivery and user-facing error states remain runtime verification points.

Journey: Synchronize and validate tenant/device context

Risk: high · machine API operations; no SPA route.

  1. Tenant client requests an API session using its client credentials.
  2. Authenticated client submits synchronization requests. The service decrypts the request, applies supported tenant-resource changes and returns an encrypted response.
  3. Client submits a MAC/serial or API-access validation request under the TenantApi policy.
  4. API resolves the tenant claim and checks tenant, branch, terminal MAC and device serial against configured SQL data.
  5. Endpoint returns the context-validation result. This repository does not establish the external biometric/identity-verification result.
Failure pathExpected handling / evidenceConfidence
Invalid machine credentialsAuthentication fails; failed-login rate limiting applies. Threshold and runtime response are not asserted.Code-backed; runtime unverified.
Missing/invalid tenant claimValidation rejects the request as an invalid token/tenant context.Explicit in ValidationController.
Unknown or cross-tenant branch/MAC/serialForeign resources must not be treated as belonging to the authenticated tenant.Service flow is code-backed; negative isolation matrix needs automated verification.
Encrypted synchronization cannot be processedRequest/response cannot complete normally; exact error contract awaits API-map verification.OpenAPI unavailable; controller/service source inspected as approved substitute.

Data lifecycle pointers: business-data-context#flow-tenant-api-validation and business-data-context#state-tenant-api-token. Contract details belong in the pending API map.

Journey: Review tenant operational logs

Risk: high · routes /logs/consultas-nr, /logs/peticiones-nr, /logs/respuestas-no-satisfactorias-nr.

  1. A TenantAdmin or UserApp signs in; tenant login redirects them to /admin-panel or its consultation-log view.
  2. User selects a consultation, request or unsatisfactory-response log view.
  3. Portal requests filtered/paginated records. Backend uses caller tenant scope and configured MongoDB log collection.
  4. Portal displays records for operational review; these reads do not modify authoritative tenant/resource records in PostgreSQL.

Unhappy paths: expired session, denied role, invalid filter/date range, unavailable MongoDB, or no matches. Policies/read-only behavior are code-backed; empty-state, paging and error recovery require a runtime session.

Boundary: the external transaction producing biometric/NR records is not traced here. The map does not claim that tenant API validation creates those logs.

Data pointer: business-data-context#flow-log-review; retention and sensitivity rules remain unverified.

Journey: Request and retrieve an ATDP export

Risk: medium-high · admin API request/download operations; matching SPA route not found in inspected route tree.

  1. Platform administrator requests an export for a tenant and range.
  2. API saves a download request as Pendiente and publishes the request identifier and range to RabbitMQ.
  3. External worker is expected to generate the PDF; API calls the worker to retrieve the document or map a service error.
  4. An authorized API caller retrieves the resulting document when available.

Failure path: request row is written before queue publication, and no compensating update was found for publish failure. The RabbitMQ consumer and subsequent status writer are outside the inspected backend; do not assert completion until that path is verified.

Data pointers: business-data-context#flow-atdp-export and business-data-context#state-atdp-download.

Cross-feature flow: Tenant readiness to machine access

Tenant creation, admin activation, credentials, resource configuration, synchronization and context validation form one readiness chain. A missing/mismatched tenant, branch, terminal or device can block an access check even when the client authenticates. The data map owns entities and state transitions; this map keeps the user-facing dependency chain.

PrerequisiteConsumer featureRisk to verify
Active tenant and valid API credentialsMachine authenticationDisabled/revoked credentials must not yield a usable tenant session.
Tenant-owned branch, terminal and device identitiesSynchronization and validationReject missing, duplicate or foreign-tenant identities.
Tenant application user and operational recordsTenant log reviewDo not expose another tenant's records.
Enabled tenant and available configurationPortal resource actionsDisabled tenant cannot use resource actions disabled by the UI.

Discovery gaps

  • The business API map is now generated from controller and route inspection, but request/response schemas and error semantics have not been independently compared with a generated OpenAPI contract. The OpenAPI MCP was unavailable during this refresh.
  • The frontend was not exercised in a running environment. Runtime messages, empty states, navigation edge cases, date filters, modals and responsive behavior remain unverified.
  • External biometric capture and identity-decision workflow is outside inspected repositories. The available validation API checks tenant/device context only.
  • Source, ownership and retention policy of NR logs are unverified; the map does not connect machine context validation to log creation.
  • ATDP RabbitMQ consumer/status writer are outside inspected backend. Queue failure can leave a persisted request pending; completion/retry path is unknown.
  • Operator invocation and real contingency failover were not located; configuration is not proof of working failover.
  • Role APIs are hidden from API explorer and explicitly inactive in SPA; role-to-account relationships and intended use need clarification.
  • Direct /dashboard has shell authentication but no nested admin role guard, while its navigation item is admin-only. Intent and non-admin deep-link behavior need clarification/runtime verification.
  • UserApp create/update UI schemas declare different username character sets. Compare with backend validation and decide whether the difference is intentional before treating either as contract.
  • No tracked automated suite was identified. Existing manual plans/reports are external to product repos; confirm which apply to this portal/API scope.
  • RNEC expansion, role assignment semantics, exact lockout thresholds and business meaning of all export statuses are not confirmed beyond cited code behavior.
  • Expected legacy personas, journeys, feature-map and SRS files were not present at their expected paths; no legacy journey content was migrated.
